title: What If We Mined the Seafloor Rocks That Make Oxygen in the Dark?

scenes.text: What if rocks on the deep seafloor make oxygen with no sunlight? Scientists think they do.
About 4,000 meters down, potato-sized metal nodules sit on the dark seabed, rich in battery metals.
A 2024 study in Nature Geoscience found oxygen being produced in that total darkness.
Researchers measured nearly one volt between nodules, close to what it takes to split seawater.
Mining companies want those nodules for electric car batteries. Mining would remove the nodules, and life that depends on them.
And these rocks take millions of years to re-form. We'd be taking them for good.
